Let \(P\) be the top vertex directly above \(A\). Let the two marked midpoints on the bottom edges from \(A\) be \(D\) and \(E\). The cutting plane passes through \(P,D,E\).

The part containing \(A\) is the tetrahedron \(A-D-E-P\).

Since \(D\) and \(E\) are midpoints of two sides from \(A\), triangle \(ADE\) is similar to the prism’s base triangle with scale factor \(\frac12\). Hence
\[
[ ADE ]=\left(\frac12\right)^2[ABC]=\frac14[ABC].
\]
The height from \(P\) to the base plane is the same as the prism height \(h\). Thus the tetrahedron’s volume is
\[
\frac13[ ADE]\cdot h
=\frac13\cdot \frac14[ABC]\cdot h
=\frac1{12}\bigl([ABC]\cdot h\bigr).
\]
But \([ABC]\cdot h\) is the volume of the whole prism, \(504\). Therefore,
\[
\frac1{12}\cdot 504=42.
\]

\boxed{42}
